full_text_zh:
[P1] 调虎离山

[P2] 虞诩是东汉著名的将领。那时候，北边的羌人经常挑起战乱。有一次，羌人又在边关烧杀抢掠，虞诩的朋友任尚被派去驻守。虞诩担心地对他说：‘这次和羌人的对战已经持续了很久，朝廷花费了许多钱财，你如果不能获胜，恐怕会被朝廷治罪呀！’

[P3] 任尚愁眉苦脸地说："之前好几位将领都没能打败羌人，真是让人头疼，我也没有什么好办法呀！"
虞诩说："羌人都骑马，一天能走几百里，来的时候像疾风骤雨，离开的时候像离弦的箭。我们都是步兵，用步兵追击骑兵，怎么能追得上？依我看——"

[P4] "我们有步兵二十多万，却只能等着羌兵打过来，还不如让这些士兵都回家去种地、养蚕。"
"那怎么行！"任尚着急了，"没有兵，羌人不是更猖狂了吗？"虞诩不慌不忙地说："可以让回家的士兵交一些钱上来。二十个人出的钱，大概就可以买一匹马。这样算下来，二十多万人出的钱，就能买一万多匹马。"

[P5] 任尚听了双眼发亮，高兴地说："再选一万多青壮年加以训练，我们就有一万多名骑兵。这样的话，我们必胜无疑啊！"
"对，这样做既能老百姓家里的田地有人种，又能打败羌人，不是一举两得的好事吗？"虞诩笑着说。
真能聊...

[P6] 按照这个计划，任尚训练出一万名骑兵，率领他们进攻被羌人占领的丁奚城，首战就大获全胜。
任尚马上把虞诩的计划写成奏章，上报给皇帝。皇帝看了也拍手称好，立刻就批准了。

[P7] 虞诩也因此立了功，被任命为武都郡太守。他带了几百名士兵，立即去上任。
去武都，最近的一条路是宝鸡的陈仓道。羌人头领听说后，便率领上千人马驻扎在陈仓道旁的山上，只等着虞诩走上陈仓道，滚石弓箭齐下，给他一个下马威！

[P8] 听说羌人设下了埋伏，虞诩手下的士兵有点慌。虞诩去上任，带的兵马不多。羌人士气正旺，又占据了有利的地势，强攻肯定打不过，怎么办呢？虞诩半路勒住了马，下令道："停止前进，就地扎营。"

[P9] 羌人看汉军还没进陈仓道，
就在山上扎了营，又派人
下山来骚扰，却被汉军一
阵乱箭给射了回去。

"不打吗？"士兵问虞诩。
"不打。"
"羌人攻过来怎么办？""严防死守。"

[P10] 这时，虞诩仔细观察着山上的羌兵。已经快到六月了，羌兵还穿着厚厚的衣服，虞诩询问探路回来的士兵：羌人来这里多久了？
"才来没几天。"士兵回答说。
"哦——那就放出消息，说我军正向朝廷请求派兵增援。"
"这消息怎么放呢？"
"对羌人不用拐弯抹角，直接喊话。虞诩笑着说。

[P11] 援兵一到，就和你们决一死战！
于是，一名身高体壮的士兵就朝山上大声喊：“喂，羌兵们听好了！我们大人已经向朝廷求援，援兵一到，就和你们决一死战！”羌兵见汉军几天不出营，以为他们真的在等援兵，于是渐渐地放松了戒备。几个头领一商量，天气热了，他们还没有单衣穿，吃的也不多了，得下山抢点东西了。

[P12] 等到大部分羌兵都出去抢东西了，虞诩瞅准时机命令道："开拔，闯关。"
山上只剩下十几个羌兵在望风，这时只能眼睁睁地看着虞诩带人进了陈仓道。
"每天行程不得低于二百里，迅速通过陈仓道。"
虞诩带着大家急匆匆地往前冲。

[P13] 半路扎营做饭时，虞诩又下令："今天每人挖两个灶坑，明天挖四个，每人每天都要多挖两个灶坑。"士兵不解地问："我们每天急行二百里，是为了甩掉羌兵，可为什么还要浪费时间多挖灶坑呢？"

[P14] 虞诩回答说："秦岭山谷只有这一条路，光靠跑是摆脱不了羌兵的。我们五百个人，今天挖一千个灶坑，明天挖两千个，后天就变成了三千个。敌人看到我们的灶坑每天都在增加，一定会认为援兵来了。他们就不再敢追了。"

[P15] 果然，羌兵见汉军的灶坑一天比一天多，就再也不敢靠近他们了。虞诩带兵顺利地通过陈仓道，到达了武都郡。虞诩镇守武都郡，赶走了羌兵，百姓过上了安宁的日子。短短两三年，武都郡就从一万户增加到了四万多户。

[P16] 于是，虞诩故意放出等待援兵的假消息，成功将羌人调离山顶，同时，在行军的路上制造援兵已到的假象，最终顺利冲出陈仓道。
羌人就像守在陈仓道上的老虎，虞诩想要顺利通过，强攻不行，只能引开羌人，调虎离山。
人呢？
full_text_en:
[P1] Lure the Tiger Away from the Mountain

[P2] Yu Xu was a famous general of the Eastern Han Dynasty. At that time, the Qiang people in the north often provoked wars. Once, the Qiang people raided and looted at the border again, and Yu Xu's friend Ren Shang was sent to defend the frontier. Yu Xu worriedly said to him: 'This battle against the Qiang has lasted for a long time. The court has spent a lot of money. If you cannot win, you might be punished by the court!'

[P3] Ren Shang said with a worried expression: "Several previous generals couldn't defeat the Qiang people. It's really headache-making, and I don't have any good ideas either!"
Yu Xu said: "The Qiang people all ride horses and can travel hundreds of miles in a day. When they come, it's like a sudden storm; when they leave, it's like an arrow released from a bow. We are all infantry. How can we possibly catch up with cavalry using foot soldiers? In my opinion—"

[P4] "We have over 200,000 infantry, but we can only wait for the Qiang troops to attack. It would be better to let these soldiers go home to farm and raise silkworms."
"How can that be!" Ren Shang exclaimed anxiously. "Without soldiers, won't the Qiang become even more rampant?" Yu Xu calmly replied, "We can ask the soldiers returning home to contribute some money. The money from twenty men can buy one horse. Calculating this way, the money from over 200,000 men could buy over 10,000 horses."

[P5] Ren Shang's eyes lit up, and he happily said, "If we select over ten thousand young and strong men for training, we will have over ten thousand cavalry soldiers. In that case, we will surely win without a doubt!"
"Right, this way, not only can the farmland in the people's homes be cultivated, but we can also defeat the Qiang people. Isn't this a win-win situation?" said Yu Xu with a smile.
Really clever...

[P6] According to this plan, Ren Shang trained 10,000 cavalrymen and led them to attack Dingxi City, which had been occupied by the Qiang people. They achieved a great victory in their first battle.
Ren Shang immediately wrote a memorial outlining Yu Xu's plan and submitted it to the emperor. The emperor read it and clapped in approval, immediately approving the proposal.

[P7] Yu Xu thus earned merit and was appointed as the governor of Wudu Commandery. He brought several hundred soldiers and immediately set out for his post.
To reach Wudu, the shortest route was the Chen Cang Pass in Baoji. Upon hearing this, the Qiang chieftain led over a thousand men and horses to camp on the mountain beside the Chen Cang Pass, waiting for Yu Xu to enter the pass, ready to shower him with rolling stones and arrows as a welcoming strike!

[P8] Heard that the Qiang had set an ambush, the soldiers under Yu Xu were a bit panicked. Yu Xu was going to take up his post, but he brought few troops. The Qiang were in high spirits and had taken a favorable position; a direct attack would surely fail. What should be done? Yu Xu pulled his horse to a halt halfway and ordered, "Stop advancing, set up camp here."

[P9] The Qiang people saw that the Han army had not yet entered the Chen Cang Pass, 
so they set up camp on the mountain and sent people down to harass them, 
but were shot back by a volley of arrows from the Han army.

"Not fighting?" the soldier asked Yu Xu.
"Not fighting."
"What if the Qiang attack?" "Defend strictly and hold fast."

[P10] At this moment, Yu Xu carefully observed the Qiang soldiers on the mountain. It was almost June, yet the Qiang soldiers were still wearing thick clothes. Yu Xu asked a soldier who had returned from scouting: "How long have the Qiang been here?"
"Only a few days ago," the soldier replied.
"Oh—then let's spread the word that our army is requesting reinforcements from the imperial court."
"How should we spread this news?"
"With the Qiang, there's no need to beat around the bush. Just shout it out," Yu Xu said with a smile.

[P11] When reinforcements arrive, we'll fight you to the death!
Then, a tall and strong soldier shouted up the mountain: "Hey, Qiang soldiers, listen up! Our commander has already asked the imperial court for reinforcements. As soon as they arrive, we'll fight you to the death!" The Qiang soldiers, seeing the Han army not leave camp for several days, thought they were truly waiting for reinforcements and gradually relaxed their guard. After a discussion, several leaders decided that it was getting hot, they still didn't have light clothes, and their food was running out, so they had to go down the mountain to seize some supplies.

[P12] When most of the Qiang soldiers had gone out to loot, Yu Xu seized the opportunity and ordered, "Advance, break through!"
Only a dozen or so Qiang soldiers remained on the mountain keeping watch; they could only watch helplessly as Yu Xu led his men into Chen Cang Pass.
"Our daily march must be no less than two hundred li. Move quickly through Chen Cang Pass."
Yu Xu led everyone forward in a hurry.

[P13] While camping halfway to cook, Yu Xu gave another order: "Today, each person digs two cooking pits; tomorrow, four; each person must dig two more pits every day." The soldiers asked in confusion: "We are marching 200 li every day to shake off the Qiang troops. Why waste time digging more cooking pits?"

[P14] Yu Xu replied: "There's only one path through the Qinling Mountains. Running alone won't get us away from the Qiang troops. We are five hundred men. Today we dig a thousand fire pits, tomorrow two thousand, and the day after, three thousand. When the enemy sees our fire pits increasing every day, they will surely think reinforcements have arrived. Then they won't dare to chase us anymore."

[P15] Sure enough, the Qiang soldiers, seeing the Han army's cooking pits increasing day by day, dared no longer approach them. Yu Xu led his troops smoothly through the Chen Cang Pass and arrived at Wudu Commandery. Yu Xu took command of Wudu Commandery, drove away the Qiang soldiers, and the people lived in peace. In just two or three years, the population of Wudu Commandery increased from ten thousand households to over forty thousand.

[P16] Thus, Yu Xu deliberately spread false news of awaiting reinforcements, successfully luring the Qiang people away from the mountain top. At the same time, he created the illusion of reinforcements arriving along the march, and finally broke through the Chen Cang Pass.
The Qiang people were like tigers guarding the Chen Cang Pass. Yu Xu wanted to pass through smoothly, but direct attack was not feasible; he could only lure the Qiang away, a strategy known as 'luring the tiger away from the mountain.'
Where are the people?
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页展示了绘本标题“调虎离山”，并配有一名古代装束男子的插图，他正做出指点的手势。
[P2] 本页介绍了东汉将领虞诩的背景，并描述了他担心好友任尚在边关作战失利，可能被朝廷治罪的情景。
[P3] 任尚因屡次无法击败羌人而苦恼，虞诩分析了敌我双方的兵力特点，指出步兵难以追击骑兵的困境，并准备提出自己的对策。
[P4] 任尚对让士兵回家种地的提议表示担忧，虞诩则提出让士兵集资购买战马的方案，以增强骑兵力量应对羌人。
[P5] 任尚对虞诩提出的训练青壮年组建骑兵的计划表示赞同，认为此举既能耕田又能打仗，是两全其美的办法。画面中，两人正在交谈，一旁的马匹则发出“真能聊”的感叹。
[P6] 本页描述了任尚采纳虞诩的计划，训练骑兵并成功攻下丁奚城，随后将计划上奏皇帝并获得批准的过程。
[P7] 虞诩被任命为武都郡太守，率兵前往上任。羌人头领得知后，在陈仓道旁的山上埋伏，准备用滚石和弓箭给虞诩一个下马威。
[P8] 虞诩率军前往上任途中，得知羌人设下埋伏，因兵力不足且敌方占据有利地形，他决定停止前进，就地扎营以应对危机。
[P9] 羌人见汉军未进陈仓道，在山上扎营并派兵骚扰，但被汉军乱箭击退。士兵询问虞诩是否迎战，虞诩下令严防死守，不主动出击。
[P10] 虞诩观察到羌兵在六月仍穿厚衣，判断其刚到不久，于是决定放出消息谎称汉军正向朝廷求援，并让士兵直接喊话传递信息。
[P11] 汉军士兵向山上的羌兵喊话，谎称已向朝廷求援，待援兵到达后将决一死战，以此麻痹敌人。羌兵因长期围困、物资短缺，放松戒备，决定下山抢夺物资。
[P12] 虞诩趁羌兵下山抢夺物资、山上守军稀少之际，果断下令进军，率军迅速通过陈仓道，成功摆脱埋伏。
[P13] 虞诩在行军途中下令士兵每天增加挖灶坑的数量，士兵对此感到不解，询问为何要浪费时间多挖灶坑。
[P14] 虞诩向士兵解释，通过每天增加挖灶坑的数量，制造汉军增援到来的假象，以迷惑羌兵，使其不敢追击。
[P15] 虞诩通过增灶计策成功迷惑羌兵，顺利抵达武都郡并击退敌军，使当地百姓安居乐业，人口迅速增长。
[P16] 本页总结了虞诩通过散布假消息和制造假象，成功诱使羌人离开山顶，从而率军顺利通过陈仓道，并用‘调虎离山’的比喻解释了其策略。
